sources.title: Foreign Ministry: eight nationalities enter Group I
sources.officialityEvidence: Bolivia’s Foreign Ministry publishes this dated announcement on its official consular-domain news site and directly names the eight nationalities added to Group I.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Los países que ingresan al Grupo I (sin requerimiento de visa) son:

sources.title: Foreign Ministry: implementation of eight-country visa removal
sources.officialityEvidence: Bolivia’s Foreign Ministry publishes this follow-up implementation announcement on its official cancilleria.gob.bo domain and repeats the eight affected nationalities.
sources.supportingExcerpt: La disposición se extiende también a ciudadanos de Sudáfrica, Bulgaria, Malta, Rumania, Emiratos Árabes Unidos, Israel y Estados Unidos.

sources.title: Foreign Ministry notice: Bolivia–Honduras tourist/visit visa suppression
sources.officialityEvidence: The Foreign Ministry publishes this dated implementation notice on its official cancilleria.gob.bo domain.
sources.supportingExcerpt: ciudadanos bolivianos y hondureños podrán transitar entre ambos países sin la necesidad de tramitar visas.

sources.title: Foreign Ministry notice: Dominican tourism visa suppression
sources.officialityEvidence: The Foreign Ministry publishes this dated incoming-Dominican tourist-entry notice on its official cancilleria.gob.bo domain.
sources.supportingExcerpt: los ciudadanos dominicanos podrán ingresar a Bolivia sin la necesidad de tramitar visa para turismo.

sources.title: Brazilian Presidency Decree 5.541: Bolivia–Brazil entry-facilities agreement
sources.officialityEvidence: Brazil’s Presidency legal portal promulgates the bilateral agreement, records its international entry into force on 16 September 2005, and reproduces its reciprocal no-visa terms.

sources.title: Foreign Ministry: current tourist visa Group I/II/III framework
sources.officialityEvidence: The Foreign Ministry publishes its current visitor-visa framework and group definitions on its official website.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Las personas de nacionalidad de los países comprendidos en el Grupo II, REQUIEREN de Visa.

policies.title: Bolivia: eight named ordinary passports added to Group I
policies.summary: The Foreign Ministry expressly says these eight nationalities entered Group I without a visa requirement. This is visa-free tourism/visitor access, not an ETA, eVisa or visa-on-arrival route.
conditions: The official announcement directly names this closed eight-nationality cohort as entering Group I without a visa requirement.
It does not establish a visa status for any unlisted nationality; no complement is inferred.

The source does not specify stay duration, entries, fee, extension, admission outcome, health, funds or onward-travel conditions. Residence, work, study, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, special-document and third-country-document routes are excluded.

policies.title: Bolivia: Honduran ordinary passports visa-free for tourism or visit
policies.summary: Bolivia’s Foreign Ministry states that Honduran and Bolivian citizens may travel between the two countries without a tourist or visit visa from 17 March 2024. This is visa-free access, not an ETA, eVisa or visa-on-arrival route.
conditions: The Ministry expressly makes the mutual tourist-or-visit visa suppression effective for Honduran citizens entering Bolivia.
The announcement refers to diplomatic, official and ordinary passports; this policy records only the ordinary-passport tourism/visit route.
No duration, entries, fee, extension, admission outcome, health, funds or onward-travel condition is inferred.

policies.title: Bolivia: Dominican ordinary passports visa-free for tourism
policies.summary: Bolivia’s Foreign Ministry states that Dominican citizens could enter Bolivia without processing a tourism visa from 2 September 2024. This is visa-free access, not an ETA, eVisa or visa-on-arrival route.
conditions: The Ministry expressly identifies Dominican citizens entering Bolivia without a tourism visa and identifies ordinary passports in the underlying agreement.

No duration, entries, fee, extension, admission outcome, health, funds or onward-travel condition is inferred. Residence, work, study, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, special-document and third-country-document routes are excluded.

policies.title: Bolivia: Brazilian ordinary passports visa-free
policies.summary: The officially promulgated Bolivia–Brazil agreement directly permits nationals of either party to enter the other without a visa and expressly preserves use of an international passport. This is visa-free access, not an ETA, eVisa or visa-on-arrival route.
conditions: This policy follows the agreement’s direct no-visa entry rule for Brazilian nationals travelling to Bolivia; it is not inferred from Mercosur membership or from a document alternative.
The agreement permits the use of an international passport even though it also provides a national-identity-document route.

It states a stay of up to 90 days, extendable for another 90 days in a year, for official, tourism or business activities. Other purpose and admission conditions remain outside this ordinary short-visitor baseline.
